title: Injection-molding draft and wall DFM starter

provenance.citation: ISO 294-4 molding shrinkage practice and general injection-molding DFM practice
provenance.note: Starter pack encodes checks with explicit rule inputs; it does not claim a universal draft or wall threshold.

terminology.definition: The taper applied to a mold face so the part can be ejected without scuffing or dragging.

provenance.note: Required draft depends on material, surface texture, feature depth and tool design.

terminology.definition: The intended uniform wall thickness of the molded part.
The melt flow length divided by local wall thickness, used as a screening indicator for fill pressure and short-shot risk.

provenance.note: A screening ratio is not a substitute for a mold-flow simulation with material data.

models.name: Draft, wall-uniformity and flow-ratio manufacturability checks

provenance.note: Rule thresholds are explicit inputs from the DFM review, never hidden defaults.

variables.description: draft angle on the mold face
minimum draft required by the DFM review

provenance.note: Angles are dimensionless in SI but must still be converted as angles, not silently mixed with radians.

variables.description: melt flow path length from gate
local wall thickness along the flow path

assumptions.statement: Minimum draft, maximum wall variation and maximum flow ratio are explicit inputs from the material/tool DFM review.

provenance.note: A missing rule input makes the check unavailable; it is never defaulted.

assumptions.statement: The part is a thermoplastic injection molding; thermoset, compression and blow molding have different rules.
Tool deflection, core shift, gate freeze and pack pressure are not modeled by these geometric checks.

provenance.note: A passing geometry check is not a moldability proof.

validity_domains.statement: Draft and wall thresholds are valid only for the specific tool, texture and ejection design that supplied them.
Flow ratio and wall rules must use the actual material grade's processing window.

property_sources.authority: Material datasheet or ISO 294-4 test, revision-bound

provenance.citation: ISO 294-4 Plastics - Injection moulding of test specimens
provenance.note: Shrinkage depends on direction, thickness and process; a single generic number is not enough.

design_rules.rule: Every ejectable face needs the minimum draft specified by the tool/material DFM review; textured or deep faces require more.

provenance.note: There is no universal draft number; the rule input carries its source.

design_rules.rule: Wall thickness variation must stay within the maximum ratio agreed at DFM review to limit sink, warp and cycle variation.
Check the flow length ratio against the material-specific limit; escalate to mold-flow simulation when it is exceeded.

manufacturing_rules.rule: Textured surfaces require additional draft because the texture depth increases ejection resistance.
Verify wall thickness and draft on the first article, not only on the CAD model.
manufacturing_rules.check: first-article dimensional report includes wall and draft

failure_modes.cause: insufficient draft, texture, undercut or excessive ejection force
failure_modes.detection: visual inspection, surface roughness, mold-trial ejection force

failure_modes.cause: non-uniform wall thickness, inadequate packing or anisotropic shrinkage
failure_modes.detection: first-article metrology, flatness and parallelism checks, mold-flow comparison

diagnostic_signatures.signature: short shot at the end of a long thin flow path
diagnostic_signatures.indicates: flow length ratio or injection pressure outside the material process window

test_methods.method: First-article dimensional inspection including wall thickness and draft
Mold trial with short-shot and pressure-drop study
test_methods.measures: fill behavior, flow ratio margin, ejection behavior

standards_mappings.scope: determination of molding shrinkage of thermoplastics

provenance.note: Metadata only; licensed text is not embedded.

standards_mappings.scope: determination of tensile properties of plastics

worked_cases.description: A nominal 2.5 mm wall varies from 2.2 mm to 2.9 mm with 0.5 degrees of draft against a 1.0 degree requirement.

inputs.name: draft_min_required
inputs.note: value supplied by the DFM review

provenance.citation: Closed-form evaluation of the DFM checks
provenance.note: The numeric values follow from the inputs; the rule thresholds are explicit inputs.

counterexamples.claim: A vertical wall with zero draft is manufacturable because CAD can represent it.
counterexamples.refutation: A zero-draft face has no ejection clearance; friction and texture can cause drag, scuffing or ejection damage even if the nominal geometry closes.

known_traps.trap: Comparing a draft angle in radians with a minimum expressed in degrees, or dropping the angle unit because it is dimensionless in SI.
known_traps.why_shallow_fails: 0.5 radians is about 28.6 degrees, not 0.5 degrees; the dimensional check passes but the physical verdict is wrong.
known_traps.guard: Carry angle units through conversion and report both the converted value and the rule source.
